findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple wiping cloths in the hand sink. Education was carried out. The rags were removed. Ensure that the all handwashing sinks in the facility are use for handwashing only. Keeping items in the hand sinks discourages proper handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer in the sani buckets were unreadable. PIC was made aware. The sanitizers were remade and tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizer is within the appropriate range at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine was observed with soil accumulations. PIC was made aware. The ice was taken out and the baffles cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ice machine baffles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the triple sink was observed to be unsealed. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the triple sink will be sealed properly.  Ensure that the caulking is re-done providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) A tray of cooked dumpling was observed being stored underdressed raw chicken to cool. Education was carried out and the dumpling tray was removed. Ensure that proper storage order is practiced to avoid cross contamination. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Multiple soda nozzles were observed with soil accumulation. PIC was made aware. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed water chestnuts being stored in the can after opening inside the prep cooler. Education was carried out. The chestnuts were placed in the appropriate storage container. Ensure that food items are stored appropriately to avoid contamination. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff members bare hands in single service containers while pouring ready to eat food items in the containers. PIC was made aware that such bare handling could lead to contamination. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable when handling ready to eat food items. Hence, hands must be washed and gloves donned in such process.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water being stored in the mop bucket. Discussed with PIC and the mop bucket was drained into the utility sink. Ensure that such wastewater is properly drained to avoid the harboring of pests and bacteria growth.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffle of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink and black molds on its surface. Discussed with PIC and an employee was instructed to note the location when cleaning the ice machine. Ensure that this item is observed and cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean and sanitized.[P]
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: A packet of shrimp was observed in a bowl of water at the top of the triple sink to be thawed. PIC was made aware of appropriate thawing methods. The bowl with the shrimp was placed under running water for appropriate thawing. Ensure that staffs are aware of the adequate thawing methods to avoid the contamination of food items. [Pf]
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: A live roach was observed under the hand sink at the end of the cook line. PIC was made aware f the presence of pest and PIC ensured that a pest control company was going to be called to handle the presence of pest. Ensure that facility is routinely checked for pest presence and activities. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to indicate the accumulation of soils and food debris.
1. Accumulated grease under the grill and oven on the cook-line.
2. Food debris under the prep cooler across from the cook-line
3. The walk-in freezer was observed to have spilled food debris on the floor. 
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that adequate cleaning will be done. Ensure that these areas are cleaned to remove their current buildup of residues and that surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there is not signed employee health reporting forms for all employees. The PIC had blank copies of the reporting forms and has some forms signed by current employees. Ensure that all employees sign employee health reporting forms. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the following food in the walk-in cooler was not protected from cross contamination during storage: (1) Raw chicken stored above sauce with a saran-warp lid that was only half covering the top and a container missing a lid; and (2) Date marking sticky notes on top of food. The above mentioned sauces with improper lids were moved from below the chicken. The sticky notes were removed from the food and stuck on the side of the containers holding the food. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Observed the standing freezer and the standing clear door cooler do not have internal thermometers. Ensure that all refrigerated food storage units have temperature meaning devices. There will be a follow-up on 07/22/2024 to ensure the sanding freezer and standing clear door coolers have thermometers. 

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.comment:
Observed batter stored in tubs sitting on the floor. Ensure that food is stored at least 6-inches off the flood to prevent contamination. The batter was moved off the floor during the inspection.

(C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: The cooler that is used to hold the par-cooked chicken and the beef is observed to be out of temperature. According to the PIC, this cooler went out of temp sometime this morning with an unknown start time. During the inspection, the cooler temperature was internally checked by probing food items, which registered at 53 degrees F with an ambient air temperature of 58 degrees F. With an unknown start time of temperature abuse, the entire cooler is being voluntarily discarded of all remaining food items. PIC is ordering a new cooler to utilize in its place. A spot check will be conducted on Monday, 7/10/23, to observe the cooler replaced, repaired, or not in use. 
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C): The employees of the facility have not completed a food handler certification course. PIC asked for a link to an ANSI accredited certification course that is offered in Chinese. The inspector will forward the PIC a link to an ANSI accredited food handler course. Each employee needs to have a food handlers and have their food handler certification in a verifiable manner.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C): Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.comment: 3-304.12: A knife was observed stored between the prep tables along the cook line. This knife was removed from service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that in use utensils are stored in a manner that prevents contamination of the food contact surface. 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The hand sink is observed to have a very loose faucet. Ensure this item is reattached to create a secure seal for the faucet attached to the sink basin.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Observed multiple employees go from one task to another without washing their hands after contamination occurs. Inspector had a discussion with the PIC about hand washing and to ensure retraining and education are given to their staff regarding hand washing. Ensure hand washing is completed to ensure contamination does not occur of the food being handled.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink was observed to have multiple rags in the basin which inhibited employees form accessing the hand sink. These rags were removed immediately and education was provided to the PIC as to why having the hand sink clear is crucial to contamination prevention. Ensure this hand sink remains clear and is only used for hand washing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket was observed to have been used with soap as there were many bubbles present. It was confirmed by the employees that soap was indeed mistakingly used instead of bleach. This bucket was immediately dumped and filled with fresh warm water and bleach at a concentration of 100ppm. Ensure the sanitizer bucket is at least 100ppm bleach to be used for sanitizing the kitchen surfaces.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Many areas in the kitchen, including, but not limited to the shelves and under hard to reach areas, are observed to be in need of a detailed cleaning. Ensure detailed cleaning is performed at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The shelving units int he back of the facility are observed to have missing or shipped paint which has exposed bare wood. THis bare wood needs to be resealed by using a sealant such  as paint to make the surface smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: In the walk-in cooler, raw chicken was observed to be stored in a container above cooked fried rice. The chicken was moved during the inspection to prevent the potential contamination of the rice. Ensure proper storage practices are followed to ensure the safety and the integrity of the food remains.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The bleach sanitizer bucket registered at a level below 50ppm when tested. Bleach was added to the solution during the inspection and registered at 100-200ppm. Ensure that the test strips are regularly utilized to ensure the sanitizer concentration is sufficient enough to accomplish the sanitization process.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There were observed multiple wiping cloths on the counter being used to wipe off surfaces and then stored on the counter surface. These rags were placed into the corrected sanitizer solution during the inspection. Ensure the rags are placed into the sanitizer solution between uses to prevent cross contamination from the rag’s surface to the object being cleaned and sanitized.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Multiple surfaces in the facility are in need of a general cleaning. These surfaces include the floor, wall, and shelving. Ensure these items are cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil and residue accumulation and the deter the presence of pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: When the inspector went to wash their hands, it was noted that there were no paper towels available. During the hand washing, a roll of paper towels was brought to the inspector. Ensure that the hand sink is always supplied with soap, paper towels, and a trash can nearby.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: It was observed during the start of the inspection that there was no sanitizer bucket made and ready to use. Inspector provided education to the facility that during any hours of operation or during any prep work there must be a sanitizer bucket available with 100-200ppm of bleach. The sanitizer bucket was created during the time of the inspection and recorded using test strips to be between 100-200ppm bleach solution.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: It was observed that the tongs in the prep table were stored with the handles touching the foods. This action was corrected by the inspector on sight and reeducating the staff was performed by the PIC on how to properly store the in use utensils to prevent contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1) 5-204.11 A HANDWASHING SINK shall be located: (A) To allow convenient use by EMPLOYEES in FOOD preparation, FOOD dispensing, and WAREWASHING areas (B) In, or immediately adjacent to, toilet rooms. On arrival, the hand sink at the back of the kitchen was difficult o reach due to a barrel being in the way with a container of food on top. Inspector moved the barrel to facilitate their own hand washing during the inspection. 
2) 6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with:
(A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. The men's bathroom was without paper towels during the inspection. The PIC stated that they ran out of the ones intended for the dispenser and had been drying their hands elsewhere. Inspector stated that all hand sinks need to be supplied adequately to facilitate hand washing. A roll of paper towels was provided during the inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) A bucket of "sweet n sour" sauce is observed under the end of the three part sink and to have floating particles on the surface. The sauce was discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
1) 3-305.12  (C) Food may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. "Sweet n sour" sauce and soaking vegetables are observed stored under the 3 part sink. This is not a safe location to store containers of food. 
2) 3-305.11  (C) Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. A container of cooked beef in the walk in cooler ia observed without a covering. PIC is instructed to ensure that all foods are adequately protected from contamination.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: (3rd REPEAT) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. No proof of completion from an ANSI approved allergen awareness course is available during the inspection. PIC stated that they forgot.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 (P) The Person in Charge shall ensure that: (O) “Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). No reporting agreements are observable at this time at the facility. Multiple reporting agreements (in Chinese) were given to the PIC during the inspection for the current employees to sign. Employees signed during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surfaces should be washed, rinsed and sanitized often enough so as to be maintained clean. The blade of the can opener was observed heavily soiled during the inspection. The can opener was moved to the 3 part sink for cleaning.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. The bleach being used in the facility does not have instructions for food contact surfaces, nor an EPA registration label. Facility sent an employee to retrieve a bleach with EPA registration label and instructions intended for food contact surfaces.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. The ice scoop is observed stored with the handle in the ice in the ice machine at the back of the facility. PIC was consulted and inspector reviewed handling practices for the in use utensils. The scoop was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. No proof of allergen awareness training for certified food managers at the time of the inspection. PIC was given the hand out related to this training provided by SCDPH and instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete this training prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM upon entering facility for complaint. CFM was called in order to answer questions regarding the complaint. Ensure a CFM is at facility during all hours of operation. CFM training paperwork was left with the PIC in order to assure no future violations occur.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items within walk-in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed several items within walk-in cooler to lack date marking including raw beef and chicken. PIC stated that these items were just prepped. PIC had food handlers cover items with syran wrap and date marking. Date marking was discussed with PIC and stressed importance of maintaining procedure throughout prep time. COS.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

Observed multiple items in facility to have no syran wrap covering items. Walk-in: raw beef and raw chicken. Bottom prep cooler: raw chicken and imitation crab sticks. Discussed having all food items covered within walk-in and bottom prep cooler in order to protect against contamination. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed in-use wiping clothes on counter near prep area. In-use wiping clothes were not stored in sanitization solution bucket. Ensure all in-use wiping clothes are held within a sani bucket at all times with appropriate concentrations of sanitizer.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be stored in-between uses in a manner that does not allow for drip drying and/or air drying. Ensure mops are stored in a manner for proper air drying such as upside down.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed raw shrimp thawing in standing water in the three compartment sink. Shrimp was probed at 70F. Cold water was started, and shrimp was taken to be peeled shortly after. 

Raw meat that had been cut at the beginning of the inspection was also observed thawing at room temperature on the speed cart. Thawing was discussed. Meat must be frozen to the chopped and then must thaw in order to add the flour mixture. PIC states that raw meat will be prepared after prep employees are finished with the shrimp.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed personal foods stored intermingled with food for the public in both the reach in freezer (foods and bowls stored in the door) and in the walk in cooler (chicken for personal use stored above foods for the public). All personal foods should be labeled and stored in a manner that does not have the potential to contaminate food for the public (below and in separate areas). 

Observed open cans of ketchup and pineapple in the bottom of the prep cooler. Once cans of acidic foods are opened, food should be transferred to a food grade container.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11. -

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed several wet wiping cloths sitting on prep surfaces in the kitchen. A sanitizer bucket is available and rags were moved to be submerged in this solution.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed two knives stored in between the prep cooler and the prep table in the kitchen. Do not store knives in areas that are hard to clean. Store knives in clean and sanitized areas.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Wall next to the ice machine is observed soiled with food splash. Clean the wall.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: No proof of allergen awareness training for certified food managers at the time of the inspection. Each certified food manager will need to complete an ANSI approved allergen awareness training program and provide proof of successful completion.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: Person in charge did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the wash, rinse, sanitize process, critical control points during the cooling process or proper cold storage organization. These items were discussed with the PIC. Handouts were left as indicated.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1) Observed raw ground beef stored above the filling for crab rangoon and whole cuts of beef in the walk in cooler. Final cooking temperatures were discussed with the PIC in relation to storage in coolers. In the process of moving this ground beef, the juices spilled on a box of broccoli. Box of broccoli was voluntarily discarded. 
2) Observed raw shell eggs and personal foods stored above cooked pork and chicken in the reach in cooler at the front. Cooler was reorganized so that personal foods and raw eggs were below all ready to eat foods and food for the public.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Store raw animal products below ready to eat foods so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Third compartment of the three compartment sink was not set up at the time of the inspection and food prep and service was steadily occurring. There were numerous knives on the magnetic strip that were soiled as well as a whole pan of utensils stored on a bottom shelf that had visible food remnants on them (appeared to be raw meat remnants). Sinks were cleaned and set up during the inspection and these items were washed, rinsed and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: Observed garlic in oil on the cook line that was reported to have been put there this morning to be probed at an internal temperature of 77F with no indication marked as to when this was removed from cold holding. A time as a control policy will need to be completed (completed during the inspection) for the house made sauces and garlic in oil mixture that is kept at ambient air throughout the day. The time needs to be marked when these are removed from cold holding and any left at the end of 4 hours will need to be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135°F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Observed a container of medicine stored intermingled with canned goods on the dry storage shelf in the back. Store medicines in designated areas away from food storage areas. Medicine was removed.
findings.citation_text: 7-207.11  (P) Medicines that are in a food establishment for the employees' use must be labeled as specified under 7-101.11 and located to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. Removed by employee. Reference 7-207.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Rice was observed soaking uncovered underneath the three compartment sink. Rice was removed during the inspection. There are also numerous other items under the sink such as fish, what appears to be chicken, and a rice noodle but these are reported to be personal. Do not store food under the plumbing.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed numerous wet wiping cloths sitting on surfaces throughout the facility. There is one sanitizer bucket prepared at the front cook line area. It was advised that the back half of the kitchen have a separate sanitizer bucket for their cloths as well.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed a trowel stored with the handle in contact with the rice. Store handles up and out of the food. 
2) Observed a knife stored in the crack between the prep table and prep cooler. Knife was removed and it was discussed that this is not a cleanable area and utensils should not be stored there.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed an ice scoop being used for scooping rice to be cracked and repaired with a wire. The area around the wire is visibly soiled. 
2) Observed the ice scoop in the ice machine to be cracked and repaired with a wire. These scoops were discarded. Replace scoops with new scoops that do not have unnecessary crevices.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11  (Pf) Food-Contact surface is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Three compartment sink had soiled, soapy water in the middle sink and the other two compartments were empty but soiled. The process for wash, rinse and sanitize was incorrectly described by the person in charge. All dishes and utensils must be washed with warm, soapy water, rinsed in plain water, and then soaked for 60 seconds in warm sanitizer water (bleach prepared to 200 ppm as indicated on test strips). Sinks were cleaned and set up correctly during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.18  (C) The wash, rinse or sanitize solution within the three compartment sink is dirty. Drain and replace solutions in these compartments so the wash, rinse and sanitize operations will not be adversely affected. Reference 4-501.18.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Walls throughout the facility are soiled--most notably to the right of the ice machine in the back. Clean the walls.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: No proof of allergen awareness training completion. Hand-out left.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No proof of certified food protection manager at the time of the spot check. Make sure to have enough CFM to cover each shift.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Chlorine bleach used for sanitizer does not have instructions for use on food contact surfaces (such as dishes, silverware) on the label nor does it have instructions on how to prepare for parts per million (ppm). Provide plain bleach that has both an EPA registration number and instructions for use on food contact surfaces as above.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: PIC was not able to identify proper cooking temperatures of chicken and did not identify the hazard associated with working with raw chicken and broccoli in close proximity where the batter from the raw chicken was in direct contact with the broccoli. These issues were discussed with the PIC, but active managerial control has room for improvement. 2-102.11(C)(6) (Pf) PIC cannot state the required food temperatures and times for safe cooking of TCS foods. Discussed related section of the food code. Reference 2-102.11(C)(6).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee on the wok line to be wrapping hands and arms in apron and then returning to food preparation. Hands must be washed at any point they may have become contaminated. Hand washing was discussed. 2-301.14  (P)  Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Trash can for the back of the kitchen area and hand washing sink is being used as a stand for large bowls and active prep of chicken and is not accessible. Trash can for hand washing sink needs to be accessible. 6-301.20 (C) A HANDWASHING SINK that is provided with disposable towels shall be provided with a waste receptacle.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed an employee scooping raw batter soaked chicken from one container into another where the batter soiled handle of one container was in contact with broccoli in an adjacent box of broccoli. Batter also splashed on the box of broccoli when doing this. Separation of prep areas for raw and ready to eat foods was discussed and raw chicken was moved to other areas. Make sure all areas are properly cleaned and sanitized after raw food prep occurs. 3-302.11  (P)  Use separate equipment/utensils when preparing ready-to-eat foods and raw meats. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1) Observed employee rinse a container in the soiled third compartment of the three compartment sink and immediately return it to service. An employee also washed knives but did not sanitize them before placing them back on the magnetic strip. All dish ware must be washed, rinsed and then sanitized. 2) Sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm bleach. No sanitizer was available in the facility as in Violation #48.  4-501.114  (P)  Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed garlic in oil mixture on the wok line at room temperature. It was discussed that this is a time and temperature control for safety food and must be held at 41F or below. This was discarded. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)  Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed numerous items in the cooling process in the facility such as chicken, rice and steamed broccoli. Chicken at the front prep table near the fryer was probed at 76F and was reported to have been cooked at 11:30 am. Rice in the walk in cooler was in a large bowl with a smaller bowl within and was probed at 119F after being cooked at 12:30pm. Chicken that is being cooked and cooled is in large heaps on the tray rack and probed at 195F. It is hard to have a clear understanding if these items are cooling properly because no time or temperatures are being written down. Most of these items are cooked well above 165F and cooled at room temperature in large batches before being placed in the walk in cooler eventually. Cooling should be done in small batches, single layers uncovered and rapidly so that foods reach 70F within the first 2 hours of the cooling process. It is unknown if this is occurring or not since foods are inadvertently being hot held for some time before they cool from cooking temperature to 135F. 3-501.15  (Pf) To cool rapidly, use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: Facility is not able to locate a stem thermometer for taking temperatures of food. Provide a stem thermometer for taking internal temperatures of food. 4-302.12  (Pf) A food thermometer is not available. Food thermometers shall be provided and readily accessible to ensure proper food temperatures. Reference 4-302.12.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Observed numerous small containers of different powders that were not labeled with the common name of the product and numerous personal items intermingled within food for the public that was not labeled. Label all items removed from their original containers and store personal foods separate from food for the public. 3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: 1) Observed rice soaking in water in an uncovered container underneath the three compartment sink. Do not store food under plumbing. Rice was discarded as there was something red on the container that appeared as though it may have gotten into the rice water as well. 2) Observed a container of granules for egg roll mix sitting with the bottom of the container in direct contact with the celery in the container below. Do not store the bottom of of containers in direct contact with food. 3-305.11  (C)  Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed several wet wiping cloths sitting on surfaces throughout the facility. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed a knife stored between the prep cooler and table. This is not an easily cleanable area. Store in use utensils in clean and sanitized areas. 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No sanitizer was available at the time of the inspection. Employee ran next door and purchased bleach. This bleach was not the correct bleach as it did not have an EPA registration number on the label or instructions for use on food contact surfaces. This was discussed before the employee left. 4-303.11 CHEMICAL SANITIZERS shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: There is a leak observed at the faucet on the left at the three compartment sink. 5-205.15  (C)  Repair plumbing according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: There are approximately 8 employees at the time of the inspection and facility only has 3 food handler certificates available. Provide food handler certificates for each employee. 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: Certified food protection manager does not have proof of allergen awareness training. Each certified food manager needs to complete an ANSI approved allergen awareness training program.
